concept: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
summary: Source-anchored research for mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: If the dump contains no data files matching --nsInclude, mongorestore restores no data for that requested namespace. (high confidence)

For a replica-set backup, mongodump --oplog captures writes during the dump; mongorestore --oplogReplay applies the captured operations after restoring the data. Capture ends when mongodump finishes and does not cover later writes. A directory dump stores the captured operations in oplog.bson. (high confidence)

For a restore without oplog replay, --nsInclude selects matching namespaces and --nsExclude removes matching namespaces. Both accept asterisk patterns. Exclusion takes precedence when both match. The documented command selects transactions.* while excluding transactions.*_dev. (high confidence)

The --oplogLimit timestamp is an exclusive upper bound: mongorestore omits entries with timestamps greater than or equal to it. It requires --oplogReplay, and MongoDB warns that manually selecting oplog entries can cause corruption or inconsistencies. (low confidence)
Use --nsFrom and --nsTo together to rename matching namespaces during restore. Each option requires its matching counterpart. (low confidence)

To restore a sharded-cluster dump, the documented procedure stops balancing, creates and pre-shards destination collections with the source shard keys, restores through mongos while excluding config.*, and restarts balancing. Using --drop after pre-sharding removes the sharding configuration. (low confidence)

Use --nsFrom with --nsTo to rename namespaces during restore. Asterisk replacements correspond linearly between the two patterns; dollar-delimited wildcard variables support nonlinear replacements. These options perform namespace renaming. (high confidence)

mongorestore --oplogReplay requires a full member dump created with mongodump --oplog. Do not combine it with --db, --collection, --nsInclude, --nsExclude, --nsFrom, or --nsTo. The implementation explicitly rejects includes, excludes, and namespace renames. The community thread also corrects a suggestion to use nsInclude with replay. (high confidence)

Sharded clusters do not support mongorestore --oplogReplay. mongodump --oplog is not a supported way to capture a sharded-cluster backup through mongos; the mongodump reference says it has no effect there and directs users to the dedicated sharded procedure. (high confidence)

The documented sharded-cluster dump procedure requires stopping the balancer, writes, and schema transformations. It stops balancing, locks the cluster via mongos, takes the dump through mongos, then unlocks and restarts balancing; its consistency condition requires following the steps exactly with no operations in progress at the start. (low confidence)

In its July 25, 2016 explanation, Percona identifies different shard backup completion times as a consistency problem: capturing each shard oplog only until its own dump finishes does not cover a common completion point. The article describes coordinating oplog recording until the last shard finishes; this historical explanation does not establish current support for replaying directly to a sharded cluster. (low confidence)
Without --oplog, a mongodump taken while writes continue does not represent a single moment in time. (low confidence)

mongodump --excludeCollection and --excludeCollectionsWithPrefix require a database specified through --db or the URI; repeat either option to exclude multiple collection names or prefixes. (low confidence)

mongodump --oplog fails if collection renames, aggregation with $out, mapReduce, user/role/privilege changes, or cluster-wide setting changes such as setDefaultRWConcern occur during the dump. (low confidence)
The documented sharded-cluster dump procedure needs MongoDB support for fsync locking through mongos: MongoDB 7.1, or the backported releases 7.0.2, 6.0.11, and 5.0.22. (low confidence)
